transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Lina (Redwood) / Evan, Priya, Carlos (Horizon)

Summary (auto): renewal + expansion check-in; Horizon considering reserved capacity and additional EU region; action items to send pricing and run benchmarks.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda — pricing for reserved, region add-on, and a technical checklist for VPC/KMS.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yep thanks, Maya. we've been ramping up traffic, saw a 3x increase last quarter so we're trying to lock in predictable unit cost and add EU region for our EU customers.
00:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): hi all, from MLOps side need to understand latency p95 on our chat infra, and also KV cache behavior when we add batching.
00:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): totally, Jonah's going to walk through runtime and then we'll talk pricing.
00:47 Speaker 4 (Jonah): hey, quick note — baseline from last run with the hosted tier, your p50 is ~85ms and p95 about 420ms for 512-token prompts, that was with shared capacity and default batching. errors spiked a bit during peak windows.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): the p95 is a bit higher than we like; our SLO target is 300ms p95 for interactive search. is that realistic with reserved capacity?
01:14 Speaker 4 (Jonah): yes, when we move to a dedicated pool and tune batching + prefix caching you should see p95 drop considerably — typically in our tests we see p95 around 180–280ms depending on model variant and quantization. for example switching to a 4-bit quantized profile plus larger instances helps.
01:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): can you remind me about KV cache behaviour across shards — we run multi-tenant prompts, will cache be isolated?
01:45 Speaker 4 (Jonah): caches are per-customer and per-model version, there can be cross-shard warmup behavior but KV keys are namespaced so you won't see leakage. sometimes the transcriber says KV "cash" in docs which is confusing, but it's KV cache.
02:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): on the commercial side — Horizon's current hosted spend is roughly $68k/month, conversion to reserved pool: we're roughly estimating a 20–30% unit cost reduction depending on commit and model mix.
02:18 Speaker 5 (Carlos): procurement question — if we go 12 months do we get better pricing vs 24 months? what's the delta?
02:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): typically 12 month reserved shows solid savings; 24 month can add another 5–8% but it depends on capacity commit. we'll put concrete numbers in the quote.
02:36 Speaker 2 (Evan): also need EU region — are there any data residency implications for logs and KV cache?
02:45 Speaker 4 (Jonah): yes, we can provision an EU cluster for you. logs and KV cache can be siloed to that region; note audit logs and S3 retention settings are configurable, we'll need to align on retention windows.
02:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): what about KMS/HSM — we need customer-managed keys and no plaintext keys in Redwood.
03:05 Speaker 4 (Jonah): we support KMS integrations — we can wrap keys via your cloud KMS or HSM; we provide envelope encryption and never store plaintext keys. will need a short runbook to integrate.
03:18 Speaker 5 (Carlos): legal will want SOC 2 docs and evidence for key controls. can you share that?
03:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, Lina will drop SOC2 attestation and our security pack. link in notes.
03:31 Speaker 6 (Lina): I will share SOC2 report and our KMS integration doc after the call.
03:37 Speaker 2 (Evan): on capacity sizing: we saw spiky traffic during demos — can you suggest burst vs reserved mix?
03:48 Speaker 4 (Jonah): recommended starting point given your metrics: reserved pool equivalent to 8x A100 (or similar) to cover baseline peak, with a small burst pool for unexpected traffic. autoscale policies can add burst capacity but it costs more.
04:03 Speaker 2 (Evan): and if we need additional slots for embeddings-heavy jobs? those are expensive tokens.
04:12 Speaker 4 (Jonah): embeddings can be routed to lower-cost quantized variants and batched heavily; that reduces per-token cost. We'll include model/quantization recommendations in the benchmark doc.
04:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): timeline question — when do you want to commit?
04:32 Speaker 5 (Carlos): procurement wants an execution plan by end of month, ideally sign in April.
04:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok we'll aim to have quote and security pack this week.
04:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): technical: we want a test-run in our EU region. can Redwood do a short pilot/bench in EU and share logs?
04:51 Speaker 4 (Jonah): yes, we can spin up a pilot cluster in EU — it's usually a 2–3 day setup for benchmark tests. we'll need sample prompts and expected traffic shape.
05:03 Speaker 2 (Evan): Priya will share prompts and a list of SLO-critical endpoints.
05:09 Speaker 3 (Priya): yup, will do by EOD Tuesday.
05:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): action items recap: Maya send pricing, Jonah run bench, Lina send SOC2/KMS docs, Priya share prompts, Carlos coordinate procurement timeline.
05:25 Speaker 2 (Evan): a couple of quick clarif — competitor comparisons, we've had RFPs with Vertex and Anthropic, what are the tradeoffs?
05:34 Speaker 4 (Jonah): Vertex gives deep cloud integration but less inference-optimized runtime; Anthropic is strong on safety but cost is higher. Redwood's pitch is serving performance + unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private which helps migrate to private later.
05:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): pricing model: hosted vs dedicated vs private — we'll show math in the quote.
06:01 Speaker 5 (Carlos): one more procurement ask — can we get a sample contract with SLAs?
06:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we'll attach a template NDA/PSA and the SLA language.
06:11 Speaker 6 (Lina): also linking our rollout policy doc in chat so Priya can see canary/A-B options for model rollouts.
06:20 Speaker 2 (Evan): ok thanks, sounds good. next call for tech deep dive after benchmark results.
06:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): great thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
